gaps.explanation: The statement figure comes from the accrual proprietary Statement of Revenues, Expenses and Changes in Net Position (trimmed p6): Charges for services 3,803,763 + Grant Loan Forgiveness 171,625 + Farm Rental 40,453 + Interest Income 14,899 = 4,030,740. The cash-basis budgetary comparison schedule (p8) prints the Combined Utilities Fund Total receipts as 4,430,740, with Grants and contributions 571,625 (detail index 15) in place of the 171,625. 571,625 - 171,625 = 400,000, which is part of the 805,321 Loan/Grant Proceeds/Loan Forgiveness on the cash flow statement (p7). Every other line agrees. The schedule is on another basis than the statement, so there is no fix.

The statement figure comes from the accrual statement (p6): Total Operating Disbursements 3,375,794 (includes Depreciation 422,756 and Amortization 154) + Tennant Deposit Expense 8,935 + Interest expense 33,985 = 3,418,714. The cash-basis schedule (p8) prints the Combined Utilities Fund Total disbursements as 4,295,269: Public works 2,953,038 + Capital outlay 1,064,794 + Debt service 277,437. Capital outlay and the 277,437 bond principal are cash outflows (p7) that are not expenses, while depreciation is not in the schedule. 4,295,269 - 3,418,714 = 876,555. The schedule is on another basis, so there is no fix.
